paragraphs.source_en: There were days when we felt that the Japanese did everything better than we did, from designing appealing new automobiles to ﬁnding new ways to guarantee quality. Japan soon bested us in manufacturing and marketing what we used to think of as basic American goods, not just cars, but TV sets, even steel. It was only a vicious recession in Japan, and the wholesale adoption of the best Japanese practices by our own ﬁrms, that allowed us to forget the sense we once had of being humiliated by Japanese economic superiority.
